faq: How many visitors do I need?
A few hundred visitors per version is a sensible minimum, and more for small differences. If your traffic is low, we test bigger changes so you still get a clear answer.
Which testing tools do you use?
Your site builder's own split tests, Google Optimize alternatives, VWO or simple traffic splits through your ad platform. We choose the lightest tool that fits.
What if the test shows no clear winner?
That is useful. It means the change does not matter much, so you can stop worrying about it. We then suggest a bolder variant, or a different part of the funnel.
Will testing lose me leads in the meantime?
A weaker version may get some visitors for a short time. We keep tests short, stop clear losers early and never test anything that could mislead people.

desc:
Offer and headline testing for lead pages compares two or three versions of a page, splits visitors evenly between them and shows which one brings more enquiries. Ecom Swift LLC plans the test, builds the versions in your own tools and explains the result in plain words.

## What is offer and headline testing?

Offer and headline testing is a fair experiment on a live page. You change one important thing, such as the headline, the free gift, the button or the length of the form. Visitors are shown the versions at random, and the system counts how many in each group take the action you want.

Because the groups see the versions at the same time, the comparison is fair. You are not comparing this month with last month, when many other things may have changed.

## Why opinions are a poor way to choose a headline

Everyone around a business has a favorite wording, and the loudest voice often wins. But the people who matter are visitors who know nothing about your preferences. Their reaction can differ sharply from what the team expects.

A test replaces the debate with evidence from real visitors. It also protects you from a common error: changing a page, seeing a small rise or fall, and crediting the change when the real cause was a different season or a different ad.

## How testing improves your lead results

Small changes to the promise, the gift or the form can change how many visitors act. A clearer headline helps people understand the offer faster. A shorter form removes effort. A stronger free offer gives hesitant visitors a reason to leave their details.

Each test also teaches you something about your audience that you can use on other pages and in ads. Testing cannot promise a lift, and a result may show that the original was already good. Even then you gain a confident answer and avoid a change that would have hurt.

## What a great test program includes

- One clear question per test, such as "Does a shorter form bring more enquiries?"
- A single main change between versions, so the cause is clear.
- An even split of visitors in your own testing tool.
- A defined goal, such as form submits or bookings.
- A minimum amount of data written down before the test begins.
- A rule against stopping early because one version looks ahead.
- A record of the exact dates and traffic sources.
- A results summary that names the winner and how sure we are.
- A note about what the result does and does not tell you.
- A suggestion for the next test.

## What we do

We begin by looking at your page and your goal, then choose the most important element to test. We write the alternative versions, such as a different headline, a different offer or a shorter form, and build them in your own page builder or testing tool. We set up the even split and the conversion goal, then run a trial visit through each version.

Once the test is live, we agree the minimum amount of traffic needed before judging. When it is reached, we write the summary in everyday language: which version won, how confident we are and what to test next. The larger packages cover several tests with new page versions, tracked goals and a roadmap, followed by a handover call.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Test the element most likely to matter first.
- Change only one thing between versions.
- Let the test run until the agreed amount of data arrives.
- Keep the traffic source the same during the test.
- Record the lesson from every round, including rounds where no offer comes out ahead.

**Avoid:**
- Stopping the test the moment one version looks better.
- Changing the page halfway through.
- Testing tiny details on a page with very few visitors.
- Running several overlapping tests on the same page.
- Reading a lucky result as a permanent rule.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a business with a landing page and steady traffic that wants proof before rewriting the page. It also helps an owner who has two competing ideas for an offer and no clear way to choose. A team about to spend more on ads will find that testing the page first makes the spend work harder.

## What we need from you

Give us the page to test, the goal you care about and any ideas you have for alternatives. Tell us which page builder and analytics tools you use. We never ask for passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or developer user, and the test and its data stay in your own accounts.
